clue.text: Cut hard and break apart

indicators.note: to cut a word is to trim off its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: hard in the sense of harsh or stern is severe

explanation.surface: Instructions for chopping something firmly until it splits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims the last E from SEVERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to divide or detach, synonyms for breaking apart.

clue.text: Combining crime, say, with academic work

indicators.note: say indicates the word for crime is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
a thesis is a dissertation written for a degree

explanation.surface: Merging wrongdoing with scholarship.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthesis is a fusion, the act of putting parts together into a whole.

clue.text: A different one frequents Alabama — or Mississippi, or Tennessee

definitions.text: A different one frequents Alabama — or Mississippi, or Tennessee

parts.words: A different one frequents Alabama — or Mississippi, or Tennessee
parts.note: each state name is dominated by a single repeated letter: A in the first, I in the second, E in the third

explanation.surface: It reads like a remark about someone who hangs out in various Southern states.
explanation.definitionFit: A, I and E are all letters of this class, each recurring through its state's name.

clue.text: With regret, take shrub down to the ground

parts.note: rue is a bitter evergreen herb or small shrub
an idiom meaning completely, entirely

explanation.surface: A gardener reluctantly cuts a bush right back to soil level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down to the ground' is the idiom 'suits me down to the ground', meaning completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruefully means sorrowfully or apologetically.

clue.text: Put top journalist onto newspaper

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece onto another places it after

parts.note: the Express is a British national daily paper
the editor, ED, heads a newspaper's journalists

explanation.surface: An instruction to assign a senior reporter to a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is the definition, in the sense of phrasing something: 'well put'.
explanation.definitionFit: Put as in worded or phrased, a synonym of the past tense verb.

clue.text: As it happens, turning up in base

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word backwards from bottom to top

parts.note: a live broadcast is shown as events occur

explanation.surface: Something emerging, by chance, at a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' looks like a throwaway phrase but means 'live'.
explanation.definitionFit: Base as in morally low or wicked.

clue.text: Between concert and party man put on cape

indicators.note: the word on goes between the two outer pieces

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms
a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Between a show and a party, a man is given a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a cloak in the surface but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a high headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Realize teenager's complaint upset mum!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: acne is the skin condition typical of adolescence
mum as in keep quiet, so the hush sound

explanation.surface: A teen's moaning has upset their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother but 'silent'. 'upset' reverses ACNE to ENCA.
explanation.definitionFit: To realize an asset is to convert it into money.

clue.text: Instrument used gin and other spirit

parts.note: a gin is a trap, so using one is trapping
rum is another distilled drink besides gin

explanation.surface: A drinker mixed gin with another spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like a drink but is a snare or trap; 'other spirit' then carries the drinking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with rattling wires underneath.

clue.text: Took out, not in

definitions.meaning: escorted someone on a romantic outing

explanation.definitionFit: To have dated someone is to have gone out with them; dated also means old-fashioned.

clue.text: State needs me leading team in modern business

indicators.note: the pair of me and team goes inside the words for modern and business

parts.note: modern means new
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: me leads, so it comes before the team

parts.note: taken as written
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that the state needs them to head a team in a cutting-edge firm.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexico is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Proceed without effort, when it's clear danger has passed

definitions.meaning: to freewheel, moving on momentum alone

definitions.text: when it's clear danger has passed
definitions.meaning: the idiom 'the ___ is clear' says no lookout or enemy is near

explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to glide along idly; the phrase 'the coast is clear' signals safety.

clue.text: Support crime

definitions.meaning: to prop or bear the weight of something
an armed robbery, as of a bank or stagecoach

explanation.definitionFit: To hold something up is to bear it; a hold-up is a robbery at gunpoint.

clue.text: Cask has excessive share of froth on beer

indicators.note: joins the two pieces in order

parts.note: to hog is to take more than one's fair share
the head is the foam on a poured beer

explanation.surface: A pub barrel that keeps pouring too much foam.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large barrel, a traditional measure for beer or wine.

clue.text: Expert performer of balancing acts

parts.note: not an acrobat but a professional who makes ledgers and books add up

explanation.definitionFit: An accountant's work is balancing the books of a business.

clue.text: No difficulty being understood in this country's terminals

indicators.note: the word for understood sits between the final letters of the two words
terminals are end points, so each word gives its final letter

parts.note: something understood without being stated is implicit

explanation.surface: A claim that problems here are easily grasped, wherever you go to its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminals' takes the last letters of 'this' and 'country' (S, Y); IMPLICIT goes 'in' between them. The 's of 'country's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplicity is ease, the absence of complication or hardship.

clue.text: Cake girl found in French church

definitions.meaning: a neoclassical church in Paris, La ___

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small sponge cake, a woman's name, and a Paris church on the Place de la ___.

clue.text: Study intensively in academic stream, right?

indicators.note: right is placed inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge, a university city

explanation.surface: A student asks whether to swot while studying in a university setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'academic stream' looks like a school class but is the River Cam at Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to revise hard at the last minute, as before an exam.

clue.text: From statesman, if 'e's Tory, it's to the right of centre

definitions.text: From statesman, if 'e's Tory, it's to the right of centre

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A political document from a Conservative statesman would lean right.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across statesMAN IF 'E'S TOry; the whole clue describes a right-wing politician's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's published programme of policies; a Tory's would sit to the right.

clue.text: Listener getting broadcast in part of Ireland

indicators.note: broadcast as in scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio listener tuning in to a programme from somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, including Dublin.

clue.text: Party with edge in marginal

definitions.meaning: a faction or team in a dispute
the border or flank of something
minor, of secondary importance, as in a lesser issue

explanation.definitionFit: Side means a faction, a flank or border, and as an adjective a minor or subsidiary matter.

clue.text: In May or June, replaced by new artisan

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: In late spring someone is swapped for a fresh craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyman is a qualified craftsman who works for another, a skilled tradesman.

clue.text: Way opera is mounted in arenas

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised, read upwards

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: An opera route being staged in big venues.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, the large sports venues.

clue.text: Showing respect to flag until ordered inside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go within the word for flag

parts.note: to flag is to droop or tire, to sag

indicators.note: put into a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone salutes the national banner until told to go indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is a banner in the surface but here the verb meaning droop; 'ordered' rearranges the letters of 'until' before they go 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saluting is greeting with a formal gesture of honour.

clue.text: Boat heads off South, keeping its flag flying

indicators.note: the heads of the words that follow, their first letters

explanation.surface: A vessel sets off southwards with its banner still raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiff is a light rowing or sailing boat.

clue.text: Just failing to get contract for something unique

definitions.meaning: in bridge, falling a single trick short of the bid

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is bridge scoring: a declarer making one trick fewer than contracted is 'one off'.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a contract down by one trick is described this way; a one-off is a unique occasion or object.

clue.text: Shape of an egg, clear to see

indicators.note: joins the two pieces in order

parts.note: an egg is slang for nought, like a duck in cricket, so the letter O
to void is to empty or clear

explanation.surface: A description of an egg's outline, easy to make out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'Shape of an egg' reads as the definition; here 'Shape' alone defines and 'to see' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid is a noun for an oval, egg-like form.

clue.text: Foreign cleric bishop encountered in Lincoln

indicators.note: the bishop is met inside the president's nickname

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US President Abraham Lincoln
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman from abroad met a bishop in the English cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city but is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbé is the French title for a priest or abbot.

clue.text: From Irish house I brought back classic tale

indicators.note: the words for Irish house and I are read in reverse

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient story carried home from a house in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War is a classic of ancient literature.

clue.text: High-flier's remarkable achievement on course

definitions.meaning: a large seabird that soars for long distances
in golf, a hole completed three strokes under par

explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a great ocean bird; in golf it means three under par on a hole, rarer than an eagle.

clue.text: Port open, we hear, needs covering

indicators.note: signals that the word for open is taken by its sound

parts.note: open as in unrestricted, free
a mantle is a cloak or covering layer

explanation.surface: A harbour's opening apparently requires shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fremantle is the port city serving Perth in Western Australia.

clue.text: Took horses to ring for cowboys' display

indicators.note: joins the second piece after the first

parts.note: rode, as in travelled on horseback
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Riders lead their mounts into an arena for a show of cowboy skills.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a show of bronco riding and roping by ranch hands.
